t:
For transfer by the Secretary of Defense to appropriations and funds available during fiscal year 1980, or thereafter, for military construction or expenses of family housing for the military departments and Defense agencies, as he determines necessary to provide funds for those appropriations or funds to eliminate losses caused by fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates that vary from budget submissions, $100,000,000, and in addition, $25,000,000 which shall be derived from Family Housing, Defense, to remain available until expended: 
Provided, That funds transferred from this appropriation shall be merged with and be available for the same purpose, and for the same time period, as the appropriation or fund to which transferred: 
Provided further, That authorizations or limitations now or hereafter contained within appropriations or other provisions of law limiting the amounts that may be obligated or expended are hereby increased to the extent necessary to reflect fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates from those used in preparing the applicable budget submission: 
Provided further, That the Secretary of Defense shall provide an annual report to the Congress on all transfers made from this appropriation: 
Provided further, That contracts or other obligations entered into payable in foreign currencies may be recorded as obligations based on the currency exchange rates used in preparing budget submissions and adjustments to reflect fluctuations in such rates may be recorded as disbursements are made.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for foreign currency fluctuation transfers by the Secretary of Defense. The only procedural element is an annual report to Congress, which stays inside the federal government; the tempting reading of that report as participation fails because Congress is not an outside party. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: Provided further, That the Secretary of Defense shall provide an annual report to the Congress on all transfers made from this appropriation

qwen_block.w: The section authorizes the Secretary of Defense to transfer funds and requires an annual report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is internal government communication, not participation by outside parties. There is no mention of consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: Provided further, That the Secretary of Defense shall provide an annual report to the Congress on all transfers made from this appropriation:

opus.w: This section appropriates money that the Secretary of Defense can transfer to cover losses from swings in foreign currency exchange rates. The only procedural step is an annual report to Congress, which may look like participation, but Congress is part of the federal government. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, given a chance to comment, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
opus.s: Provided further, That the Secretary of Defense shall provide an annual report to the Congress on all transfers made from this appropriation

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress. Congress is an internal part of the federal government, so this is intra-governmental reporting, not participation with outside entities. There are no requirements for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal parties.
qwen_chat.s: Provided further, That the Secretary of Defense shall provide an annual report to the Congress on all transfers made from this appropriation:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the Secretary of Defense to provide an annual report to Congress constitutes participation because it involves communication with an external body. However, Congress is part of the federal government (legislative branch), so reporting to it is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
